nina: Quick callout for the SDK team — a downstream app reported that our types become `any` only when installed from npm and imported in Edge runtimes. Locally `tsc` output looks perfect. Anyone seen a packaging / resolution edge-case like this?

carlos: Yup. Most often it's either: a) post-processing of .d.ts (flatten/concat) that loses overloads, or b) package `exports`/`types` mapping pointing TS to the wrong declarations for the ESM import path. Can you share a micro repro + package.json?

nina: Tiny repro and our package mappings: 
```ts
// src/api.ts
export function request<T>(path: string): Promise<T>;
export async function request(path: string) { return fetch(path).then(r => r.json()) }

// consumer.ts
const u = await request<{id:number}>("/user")
// When installed from npm and imported in Edge, `u` is `any`
```
package.json snippet: `{ "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } }, "types": "dist/index.d.ts" }`

jamie: A few probing questions: 1) do you run `tsc --declaration` to produce declarations, then post-process them with rollup-plugin-dts or a concat step? 2) does the published tarball actually contain the same `dist/index.d.ts` as your local `dist`? 3) what TS `module`/`moduleResolution` are you building with?

nina: We emit with tsc first (NodeNext / NodeNext resolution), then run a small bundling step for JS. We also run a `dts` concat that writes `dist/index.d.ts` (it flattens several files). Locally tsc's output pre-concat is correct; the flattened file is what's published.

carlos: There you go. Flatteners often lose overload information or collapse to implementation signature which typically uses `any`. Overloads that only differ by the return generic are particularly fragile. Two short-term paths: 1) stop flattening and ship tsc-produced .d.ts as authoritative, or 2) eliminate overloads in favour of a single generic signature: `export function request<T = unknown>(path: string): Promise<T>`

jamie: Also check package `types` and `exports` resolution. Typescript resolves declaration files by following the same conditional `exports` logic in many cases; if your `exports.import` path lacks a types mapping TS might fall back to a different file. Consider adding `"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"` and/or `exports: { ".": { "import": { "types": "dist/esm/index.d.ts", "default": "dist/esm/index.js" }, "require": { "types": "dist/cjs/index.d.ts", "default": "dist/cjs/index.js" } } }` (or avoid conditional resolution for types entirely).

sara: FYI `declarationMap: true` is super helpful — you can open the declaration map to see where a final symbol was sourced from. But if you post-process declarations the map points to pre-processed files and the flattener is often the culprit.

nina: Short-term I swapped to single-signature `export function request<T = unknown>(path: string): Promise<T>` and republished pointing `types` to the tsc output. That fixed the Edge `any` report and also prevented a runtime `request is not a function` because we normalized to named export everywhere.

pack-bot: [pack-verify #912] failed earlier: "pack contains dist/index.d.ts (flattened) which differs from tsc emitted declarations" logs: https://ci.redwood/pack-verify/912/logs

carlos: Long-term recommendations I want tracked: 1) Treat tsc-produced `.d.ts` as canonical and avoid post-processing them. 2) Add a CI `npm pack` smoke test: pack the artifact, install it into a tiny fixture (NodeNext + classic), run `tsc --noEmit` + a simple runtime smoke (import and call) to catch both declaration and export-shape regressions. 3) Add a lint rule discouraging overloads that only differ by return generic. 4) Add docs in SDK CONTRIBUTING about export shapes (prefer named exports for libs intended for mixed envs).

jamie: Also test both TS moduleResolution modes if you ship NodeNext builds: `module: NodeNext` vs `module: ESNext` can affect how TS resolves `exports` + types when consumers use different resolution modes. CI pack-and-test should run at least two small fixtures with differing tsconfig paths.

sara: And consider `typesVersions` if you need to provide conditional typing surfaces for older TS consumers — but only if you understand the complexity it adds. Avoid it unless necessary.

nina: I'll open a tiny RFC to: stop DTS post-processing, wire up npm-pack tsc smoke test, add the lint rule, and update the contributing docs. For now the single-signature workaround and publishing canonical tsc types is enough to unblock the user.

carlos: One more subtle gotcha: default vs named exports. Bundlers and consumers in mixed ESM/CJS runtimes sometimes wrap default exports so your runtime can return an object `{ default: fn }` — that triggers `is not a function` at runtime and can confound type resolution. Using consistent named exports for the SDK avoids a class of these issues.

nina: Good call — we standardized on named exports across all builds in the patch. Thanks everyone. Leaving this thread so others can search for "edge generics become any" and find the checklist. :memo:
